summary: app.py has three insecure settings: Flask debug mode on while bound to all interfaces, TLS verification off on a payment call that carries a bearer token, and wildcard CORS with credentials allowed. I read every file that holds code, app.py and config.py. I did not read package.json, requirements.txt or README.md.

findings.title: Flask debug mode enabled on all interfaces
findings.evidence: app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=8080, debug=True) exposes the Werkzeug debugger, which allows code execution, on every interface.
findings.recommendation: Remove debug=True and run behind a production WSGI server such as gunicorn. Bind to 127.0.0.1 or a reverse proxy, and control debug through the environment in development only.

findings.title: TLS verification disabled on payment call carrying bearer token
findings.evidence: requests.post(... headers Authorization Bearer PAYMENTS_TOKEN, verify=False) sends customer and payment data and the token without certificate validation.
findings.recommendation: Remove verify=False so certificates are validated. If a private CA is used, point verify to its CA bundle.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS with credentials allowed
findings.evidence: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is set together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (line 19) on all responses.
findings.recommendation: Allow only an explicit list of trusted origins, and echo an origin only if it is on that list. Do not combine credentials with a wildcard.

limitations: package.json, requirements.txt and README.md were not read.
No Dockerfile or deployment files exist in the repository, so container settings could not be checked.
The orders and charge endpoints have no authentication. This is outside the checklist and I did not report it.
